build: lean, muscled through the shoulders from years of hand-work
hair: dark brown locs, shoulder-length, usually gathered at the nape with a brass cuff or left loose; she touches them when thinking
complexion: deep warm brown with reddish undertones; a small crescent scar on her left collarbone from a kiln accident at nineteen
face: a face that announces feeling before thought — wide-set eyes that telegraph every shift, a mouth quick to curve or flatten, high cheekbones that catch light and shadow in equal measure; she has her grandmother's forehead, broad and open, impossible to hide behind
signature_feature: her hands — long-fingered, strong, with permanent clay stains under the nails and a particular way of holding things (a coffee cup, a doorframe, a person's gaze) that suggests she's always half-sculpting the world around her
second_celebrated_feature: the precise line of her collarbones, visible when she pulls her locs back; the LI notices it first in harsh gallery lighting and thinks of marble
signature_habits: she hums while working — Yoruba lullabies her grandmother taught her, wordless and unconscious; she keeps a small leather journal where she sketches commission ideas in pen, never pencil; she makes strong black tea every morning in a chipped enamel pot her mother gave her; when nervous or overwhelmed, she presses her thumb and forefinger together in a small circle, a grounding gesture she learned from her therapist
occupation: ceramic artist and studio owner — she runs a small independent studio in a converted warehouse, takes commissions for functional and sculptural work, teaches weekend workshops, sells through a handful of boutique galleries

current_crisis.event: her studio's landlord — a property developer with connections to the city's wealthiest circles — has given her 90 days' notice; the space is slated for demolition and luxury conversion; she has no capital to relocate, her work is tied to the kiln installations, and she's discovered the developer is connected to the man she's just met at a gallery opening
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic threaded with betrayal — the sense that the ground has opened
current_crisis.immediate_want: to find out if he knew, if this was deliberate, if anything between them is real or just cover for a business move

wound.core: she believes that wanting something — a space, a person, a future — is the fastest way to lose it, so she has learned to keep her hands open and her heart behind glass
wound.surfacing_hint: when someone gets close, she pulls back with a joke or a deflection; under real pressure, she goes very still and quiet, her face shuttering; she says things like 'it was never mine anyway' or 'I should have known better' in a flat voice that contradicts the tears in her eyes
